notes: UWP app launched via uwp-app-runner (window 'RadioManager C# SDK Sample'); the runner's verify stage was impatient (ok:false, no crash signature) but the app genuinely ran and was captured. WinUI app built and ran (PID 38584). Structural gate (Compare-Parity) returned PASS 100/100, but the checklist had 0 controls/0 actions (radio rows are runtime-generated), so it did not catch the missing Status area — found by direct UIA + visual comparison. Radio toggles are hardware/permission-gated and empty in both apps, so per-radio ToggleSwitch behavior is unverifiable on this machine.

features.name: Toggle Radios navigation item
features.note: Both apps show the '1) Toggle Radios' navigation entry and open the scenario page when selected.

features.name: Scenario description text
features.note: Both show the 'Description:' header and 'Enumerate Radios, and display toggles for each one'.

features.name: Radio enumeration list with per-radio toggle
features.note: Radio list content area is empty in both apps (no controllable radios / access not granted). WinUI OnNavigatedTo code mirrors the UWP handler. Per-radio ToggleSwitch behavior is hardware-gated and cannot be exercised on this machine, so the empty state matches the UWP ground truth.

features.name: Status notification area
features.note: UWP shows a static 'Status:' label plus the error banner 'App is not allowed to control radios.'. In WinUI the StatusPanel (StatusLabel + StatusBorder + StatusBlock) is defined in MainPage.xaml but does not render — absent from both the UIA capture and a live depth-8 inspect. The status feedback area is missing entirely.
